title: Money
description: Class 5 IMO — Money: profit and loss with percentages, simple interest (SI = P×R×T/100), the unitary method, and bills with discounts.

topics.title: Profit & Loss with Percentage
topics.concept:
Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP, where CP is the cost price and SP the selling price. To find profit percent, use (profit ÷ CP) × 100; for loss percent, use (loss ÷ CP) × 100.

If CP = ₹100 and SP = ₹120, profit = ₹20 and profit% = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%.

examples.problem: CP = ₹100, SP = ₹120. Find the profit and profit%.
CP = ₹200, SP = ₹150. Find the loss and loss%.

recap: Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP.

quiz.q: CP = ₹50, SP = ₹60. What is the profit percent?
CP = ₹100, SP = ₹80. What is the loss percent?

topics.title: Simple Interest
topics.concept:
When money (the principal P) is kept in a bank, it earns simple interest. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where R is the rate per year (%) and T is the time in years.

For P = ₹1000, R = 5% and T = 2 years: SI = (1000 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100 = ₹100.

examples.problem: Find the simple interest on ₹1000 at 5% for 2 years.
Find the simple interest on ₹2000 at 10% for 1 year.

recap: P = principal, R = rate per year, T = time in years.

quiz.q: Find the SI on ₹500 at 10% for 2 years.
Find the SI on ₹1000 at 4% for 3 years.

topics.title: Unitary Method, Bills & Discounts
topics.concept:
The unitary method finds the value of one item, then scales up. If 5 pens cost ₹100, one pen costs ₹20, so 8 pens cost ₹160.

A discount is a percentage off the price. A 10% discount on ₹500 means ₹50 off, so you pay ₹450.

examples.problem: 5 pens cost ₹100. What do 8 pens cost?
A ₹500 item has a 10% discount. What do you pay?

recap: Unitary method: find the value of one, then multiply.
Price after discount = price − discount amount.

quiz.q: 3 kg of rice cost ₹150. What do 5 kg cost?
A ₹400 item has a 20% discount. How much is taken off?
